words.mm: ခံနိုင်ရည်ရှိသော
words.meaning: Able to recover quickly after something bad happens.
words.example: The town was resilient and reopened its markets a week after the flood.

words.meaning: To make something bad less serious.
words.example: Clearing dry grass helps mitigate the risk of fire.

words.meaning: To move people away from a dangerous place.
words.example: Officials evacuated the riverside homes before the water rose.

words.mm: ကြိုတင်ခန့်မှန်းချက်
words.meaning: A statement about what is likely to happen, especially with the weather.
words.example: The forecast says heavy rain will arrive tonight.

words.mm: မတည်ငြိမ်သော
words.meaning: Likely to change suddenly and without warning.
words.example: Oil prices were volatile all week.

words.mm: အခြေခံအဆောက်အအုံ
words.meaning: The basic systems a place needs, such as roads, power and water.
words.example: The storm damaged roads, bridges and other infrastructure.

words.mm: ရေရှည်တည်တံ့သော
words.meaning: Able to continue for a long time without causing harm.
words.example: The village switched to a more sustainable way of farming.

words.meaning: To discuss something to reach an agreement.
words.example: The two companies negotiated a new price.

words.mm: အပစ်အခတ်ရပ်စဲရေး
words.meaning: An agreement to stop fighting.
words.example: Both sides agreed to a short ceasefire.

words.mm: လူသားချင်း စာနာထောက်ထားမှုဆိုင်ရာ
words.meaning: Concerned with helping people who are suffering.
words.example: Humanitarian groups sent food and medicine.

words.meaning: A general rise in prices over time.
words.example: Inflation made rice and cooking oil more expensive.

words.mm: စိစစ်ကြည့်ရှုမှု
words.meaning: Careful and close examination.
words.example: The new rules are under public scrutiny.

words.mm: ယခင်က မဖြစ်ဖူးသော
words.meaning: Never having happened before.
words.example: The heat this year was unprecedented.

words.mm: မမျှော်လင့်သည့် အခြေအနေအတွက် ကြိုတင်ပြင်ဆင်မှု
words.meaning: A plan for something that might happen.
words.example: Every fire station needs a contingency plan for power cuts.

words.mm: ထိခိုက်လွယ်သော
words.meaning: Easily hurt or harmed.
words.example: Older people are more vulnerable in extreme heat.

words.mm: နေရာချထား စေလွှတ်သည်
words.meaning: To send people or equipment somewhere for a job.
words.example: The city deployed extra fire trucks during the festival.

words.mm: လုံ့လဝီရိယရှိသော
words.meaning: Working hard and with care.
words.example: She is a diligent student who never misses a class.

words.mm: ချင့်ချိန်ဆင်ခြင်တတ်သော
words.meaning: Careful and wise about the future.
words.example: It is prudent to keep some savings for emergencies.

words.mm: အသေးစိတ် ဂရုစိုက်သော
words.meaning: Paying very close attention to every detail.
words.example: The engineer kept meticulous records of every test.

words.meaning: To keep trying even when it is difficult.
words.example: He persevered and passed the exam on his third try.

words.meaning: The quality of being honest and having strong morals.
words.example: People trust her because of her integrity.

words.mm: ပွင့်လင်းမြင်သာသော
words.meaning: Open and easy to understand, with nothing hidden.
words.example: The council promised a transparent budget.

words.mm: တာဝန်ခံရသော
words.meaning: Responsible for your actions and expected to explain them.
words.example: Leaders should be accountable to the public.

words.mm: သဘောတူညီချက်
words.meaning: General agreement among a group.
words.example: The team reached a consensus after a long meeting.

words.mm: ခွဲဝေချထားသည်
words.meaning: To give a share of something for a purpose.
words.example: The government allocated money for new hospitals.

words.mm: ရုတ်တရက် မြင့်တက်ခြင်း
words.meaning: A sudden, large increase.
words.example: There was a surge in demand for fans during the heatwave.

words.mm: ရုတ်တရက် ထိုးကျသည်
words.meaning: To fall very quickly.
words.example: Temperatures plummeted after the storm.

words.mm: ပိတ်ဆို့အရေးယူမှု
words.meaning: An official penalty placed on a country or group.
words.example: New sanctions blocked some trade with the company.

words.mm: အကောက်ခွန်
words.meaning: A tax on goods coming into or leaving a country.
words.example: The new tariff raised the price of imported cars.

words.meaning: The amount by which spending is more than income.
words.example: The country ran a budget deficit last year.

words.mm: ဆန်းသစ်တီထွင်မှု
words.meaning: A new idea, method or product.
words.example: Drones are an innovation in firefighting.

words.meaning: No longer used because something newer exists.
words.example: Paper maps are becoming obsolete for many drivers.

words.meaning: To expect something and prepare for it.
words.example: We anticipate heavy traffic before the holiday.

words.mm: အန္တရာယ်
words.meaning: Something that could cause harm.
words.example: Loose wires are a fire hazard.

words.mm: ကြိုတင်ကာကွယ်မှု
words.meaning: Something done to prevent harm before it happens.
words.example: As a precaution, the school closed early.

words.mm: နောက်ဆက်တွဲ အကျိုးဆက်
words.meaning: The period after a disaster and its effects.
words.example: In the aftermath of the earthquake, volunteers cleared the roads.

words.mm: အကြီးအကျယ် ပျက်စီးစေသော
words.meaning: Causing very great damage or sadness.
words.example: The cyclone had a devastating effect on the coast.

words.mm: ပြန်လည်ဖြည့်တင်းသည်
words.meaning: To fill something up again.
words.example: The station replenished its water tanks after the fire.

words.mm: ကရုဏာ
words.meaning: Kindness and care for others who are suffering.
words.example: The monks showed great compassion to the flood victims.

words.mm: ကျေးဇူးသိတတ်မှု
words.meaning: The feeling of being thankful.
words.example: She wrote a letter of gratitude to her teachers.

words.meaning: Not proud; not thinking you are better than others.
words.example: Despite his success, he stayed humble.

words.mm: လက်တွေ့ကျသော
words.meaning: Dealing with problems in a practical way.
words.example: We need a pragmatic solution, not a perfect one.

words.mm: အဓိပ္ပာယ် မရှင်းလင်းသော
words.meaning: Having more than one possible meaning.
words.example: The message was ambiguous, so we called to check.

words.mm: ယုတ္တိရှိရှိ ဆက်စပ်သော
words.meaning: Clear and logical.
words.example: He gave a coherent explanation of the plan.

words.mm: အသေးစိတ် ရှင်းပြသည်
words.meaning: To explain something in more detail.
words.example: Could you elaborate on your idea?

words.mm: ထောက်ခံသည်
words.meaning: To publicly support someone or something.
words.example: Several doctors endorsed the new health campaign.

words.mm: လက်တွေ့ လုပ်ဆောင်နိုင်သော
words.meaning: Possible and practical to do.
words.example: Building the bridge in one year is not feasible.

words.mm: မလွဲမသွေ ဖြစ်မည့်
words.meaning: Certain to happen and impossible to avoid.
words.example: Some delays are inevitable in the rainy season.

words.mm: မဖြစ်မနေ လိုက်နာရမည့်
words.meaning: Required by a rule or law.
words.example: Wearing a helmet is mandatory on this site.

words.mm: ကြိုတင်လုပ်ဆောင်တတ်သော
words.meaning: Acting early to prevent problems.
words.example: A proactive manager fixes problems before they grow.

words.mm: တွန့်ဆုတ်သော
words.meaning: Not willing to do something.
words.example: He was reluctant to leave his home during the flood.

words.meaning: Not giving up easily.
words.example: The tenacious rescuers searched all night.

words.mm: ဖွံ့ဖြိုးရှင်သန်သည်
words.meaning: To grow or develop well.
words.example: Small shops thrive near busy markets.

words.mm: အားနည်းအောင် ထိခိုက်စေသည်
words.meaning: To slowly weaken something.
words.example: Rumours can undermine trust in a team.

words.mm: သတိဝီရိယ ရှိသော
words.meaning: Watching carefully for danger.
words.example: Stay vigilant during thunderstorms.

words.mm: စေတနာကောင်းသော
words.meaning: Kind and wanting to help others.
words.example: A benevolent donor paid for the new school roof.

words.meaning: Honest and direct.
words.example: Thank you for your candid feedback.

words.mm: ခွဲခြားသိမြင်သည်
words.meaning: To notice or understand something that is not obvious.
words.example: It was hard to discern the road through the heavy rain.

words.mm: စာနာနားလည်မှု
words.meaning: The ability to understand how someone else feels.
words.example: Good nurses show empathy to their patients.

words.meaning: Careful not to waste money.
words.example: Her frugal habits helped her save for a house.

quotes.text: Hatred is never appeased by hatred in this world. By non-hatred alone is hatred appeased. This is a law eternal.
quotes.source: Dhammapada, verse 5, translated by Acharya Buddharakkhita

quotes.text: Though one may conquer a thousand times a thousand men in battle, yet he indeed is the noblest victor who conquers himself.
quotes.source: Dhammapada, verse 103, translated by Acharya Buddharakkhita

quotes.text: Overcome the angry by non-anger; overcome the wicked by goodness; overcome the miser by generosity; overcome the liar by truth.
quotes.source: Dhammapada, verse 223, translated by Acharya Buddharakkhita

quotes.text: To avoid all evil, to cultivate good, and to cleanse one's mind — this is the teaching of the Buddhas.
quotes.source: Dhammapada, verse 183, translated by Acharya Buddharakkhita

quotes.text: Health is the highest gain. Contentment is the greatest wealth. A trustworthy person is the best kinsman. Nibbana is the highest bliss.
quotes.source: Dhammapada, verse 204, translated by Acharya Buddharakkhita

quotes.text: Irrigators regulate the rivers; fletchers straighten the arrow shaft; carpenters shape the wood; the wise control themselves.
quotes.source: Dhammapada, verse 80, translated by Acharya Buddharakkhita

quotes.text: Just as a solid rock is not shaken by the storm, even so the wise are not affected by praise or blame.
quotes.source: Dhammapada, verse 81, translated by Acharya Buddharakkhita

quotes.text: Let none find fault with others; let none see the omissions and commissions of others. But let one see one's own acts, done and undone.
quotes.source: Dhammapada, verse 50, translated by Acharya Buddharakkhita

quotes.text: One truly is the protector of oneself; who else could the protector be? With oneself fully controlled, one gains a mastery that is hard to gain.
quotes.source: Dhammapada, verse 160, translated by Acharya Buddharakkhita

quotes.text: Heedfulness is the path to the Deathless. Heedlessness is the path to death. The heedful die not. The heedless are as if dead already.
quotes.source: Dhammapada, verse 21, translated by Acharya Buddharakkhita

quotes.text: By effort and heedfulness, discipline and self-mastery, let the wise one make for himself an island which no flood can overwhelm.
quotes.source: Dhammapada, verse 25, translated by Acharya Buddharakkhita

quotes.text: Waste no more time arguing about what a good man should be. Be one.
quotes.source: Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 10.16, translated by Gregory Hays

quotes.text: The best revenge is not to be like that.
quotes.source: Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 6.6, translated by Gregory Hays

quotes.text: We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
While we are postponing, life speeds by.
quotes.source: Seneca, Letters to Lucilius, letter 1, translated by Richard Gummere

quotes.text: Men are disturbed not by the things which happen, but by the opinions about the things.
quotes.source: Epictetus, Enchiridion 5, translated by George Long

quotes.text: A journey of a thousand li commences with a single step.
quotes.source: Tao Te Ching, chapter 64, translated by James Legge

quotes.text: When you know a thing, to hold that you know it; and when you do not know a thing, to allow that you do not know it; this is knowledge.
quotes.source: Confucius, Analects 2.17, translated by James Legge

history.title: Burma became independent
history.body: Burma left British rule and became an independent republic on 4 January 1948.

history.title: The Panglong Agreement was signed
history.body: Leaders from the Shan, Kachin and Chin hills agreed with Aung San to work together for independence.

history.title: Martyrs' Day
history.body: Aung San and members of his cabinet were assassinated in Yangon. The day is remembered every year as Martyrs' Day.

history.title: Cyclone Nargis hit Myanmar
history.body: Cyclone Nargis struck the Ayeyarwady Delta and Yangon, causing one of the worst natural disasters in the country's history.

history.title: The Mandalay earthquake
history.body: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake on the Sagaing Fault struck near Mandalay, causing heavy loss of life and damage.

history.title: The Bagan earthquake of 1975
history.body: A strong earthquake damaged many of the ancient temples of Bagan.

history.title: Bagan earthquake of 2016
history.body: A magnitude 6.8 earthquake damaged hundreds of temples in Bagan.

history.title: The Bago earthquake
history.body: A major earthquake struck Bago and was also felt strongly in Yangon.

history.title: The Ava earthquake
history.body: A powerful earthquake struck the royal capital of Ava and damaged many buildings.

history.title: U Thant led the United Nations
history.body: U Thant of Burma became acting Secretary-General of the United Nations, the first Asian to hold the post.

history.title: The 1920 university boycott
history.body: Students protested against the University Act. The start of the boycott is now remembered as National Day.

history.title: The Sixth Buddhist Council opened
history.body: The Sixth Buddhist Council opened in Yangon to recite and check the Pali Canon.

history.title: Burma was separated from India
history.body: Under British rule, Burma became a separately governed colony instead of a province of India.

history.title: Mandalay was founded
history.body: King Mindon founded Mandalay as his new royal capital in 1857.

history.title: The Fifth Buddhist Council
history.body: King Mindon hosted the Fifth Buddhist Council in Mandalay, and the Pali Canon was carved on marble slabs at Kuthodaw Pagoda.

history.title: The Konbaung dynasty began
history.body: Alaungpaya founded the Konbaung dynasty, the last royal dynasty of Burma.

history.title: Anawrahta became king of Pagan
history.body: Anawrahta became king and built Pagan into the first empire to unite much of the Irrawaddy valley.

history.title: Mrauk U became a royal capital
history.body: King Min Saw Mon founded Mrauk U, which became the capital of a powerful Arakanese kingdom.

history.title: The First Anglo-Burmese War began
history.body: War between Burma and British India began in 1824 and ended with Burma losing Arakan and Tenasserim.

history.title: The Third Anglo-Burmese War
history.body: British forces took Mandalay and sent King Thibaw into exile, ending the Burmese monarchy.
